answer: A harbor only admits ships with a logged voyage history, and an agent economy can do the same: every agent must build a public work record before taking high-value jobs. New identities start at the horizon, limited to small tasks whose results are checked by peers. Trust rises slowly toward a summit, because each completed job adds a small verified increment while failures cut it sharply. A Sybil attacker must therefore pay the full cost of real, useful work for every fake identity, and one detected forgery burns the whole climb, so thousands of cheap identities buy no influence.
